head: 056341c30d15157d941566c90193c9d384b51d45
reviewed_facts: core DeviceKey private canonical String; exact virtual names or physical/native usb-64lowerhex, backend namespaces distinct; typed serde and FromStr validate; no raw BusID authorizer.

Constructor errors intentionally now core::Error; transport public type paths reexport same shared types; existing mixed-error TLS test functions use boxed error and key-list collect was explicitly changed to rustusb_core::Result.

secure PreludeWire/MappingWire/DeviceMapping strict serde fields, mandatory schema 1, 4-byte BE length before allocation, prelude4096/catalog8192, explicit 16-entry mapping visitor and unique key plus BusID.

Catalog client reads one mapping and standard DEVLIST; unique BusIDs from standard parser plus equal length and remove-from-map establish one-to-one key/address relation; no VIDPID/first-device inference.

IMPORT writes exactly standard40 bytes after selected stablekey prelude; BusId typed length<32 bounds copy. It reads exactly8+312 successful reply bytes, validates opcode/version/status and all returned header fields/count against selection; copies known interface tuples because standard IMPORT reply has no interface records. No BufReader or read_to_end consumes trailing URBs.
Each codec write_all+flush inside one five-second timeout; higher-level discover/import additionally have whole management timeout. Errors retain static contexts, not input/credential bytes.
Extracted device_header preserves old DEVLIST field parsing and MAX_INTERFACES checks; failure evaluation order is earlier header/path validation but accepted metadata semantics unchanged.

Config validates real nonzero broker euid, all root-owned non-group/other-writable parents, non-symlink regular nlink1 files, root public ownership, private root-or-broker0600, NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK plus bounded max+1 reads and same dev/inode/mode/uid/gid/nlink/size/mtime/ctime before/open/after/path checks.

Config policy1..16 unique typed pool, principal rules subset pool, finite certificate paths/bytes and pin syntax; strict client Peer validates DNS/IP and nonzero port, separate validated PKI server_name. Configuration APIs do not confer helper role.

Config fixture-only Context changes trusted fixture root and owner only in private cfg(test) paths; public production system context still root-parent rules and actual UID. Production path tests do not treat /tmp as root trusted.
limitations: No Cargo/test/QEMU or repository edits by reviewer; new tests are source only until root runs them.

Standalone DeviceKey serde allocates its input String; actual protocol/config entry points cap enclosing bytes first. This review does not claim an independent parser allocation limit for arbitrary external serde use.
Config file identity comparison is not atomic multi-file credential reload or defense against malicious root/same broker UID. Root parents are the ordinary-UID replacement boundary.
Config fixtures test predicates and real regular-file I/O, not actual root-managed positive hierarchy, synchronous kernel I/O deadlines, or adversarial root TOCTOU.
Generic secure codec requires caller-supplied authenticated stream; it intentionally cannot itself prove TLS, broker OS role, Native lifecycle or full secure USB acceptance.
Constructor error type is an intentional core API migration, not a promise of source compatibility for code explicitly requiring rustusb_transport::Error.
